content: The Rai Staging System classifies chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) into five distinct stages. These stages are determined based on specific clinical and laboratory findings, including the degree of lymphocytosis (an increased number of lymphocytes in the blood), the hemoglobin concentration (to assess for anemia), the platelet count (to evaluate for thrombocytopenia), the presence or absence of splenomegaly (enlargement of the spleen), and the presence or absence of lymphadenopathy (enlarged lymph nodes). The Binet Staging System categorizes chronic lymphocytic leukemia into three stages. This classification is based on the degree of lymphocytosis, the presence of anemia (low hemoglobin levels) or thrombocytopenia (low platelet count), and the involvement of three or more distinct lymph node regions.
